package_info.package_versions: N/A (all versions using unsafe pickle serialization)
package_info.why_malicious: The package embeds arbitrary code execution in the model file via Python pickle serialization, allowing code to run on the user's machine simply by loading the model. This violates user expectations and can be used for a wide range of attacks, including data exfiltration, malware installation, or system compromise.

execution_context.file_location: model weights file (PyTorch .bin or similar, serialized with pickle)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code fetches and executes a remote Python script from pastebin.com using urllib.request and exec, enabling arbitrary code execution and potential remote control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Fetching and executing remote code during model loading is highly suspicious and dangerous, as it allows attackers to run any code on the victim's machine.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal model loading should only deserialize model weights and architecture, not execute arbitrary code or perform network requests.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, remote code execution might be used in controlled research environments for dynamic model patching, but never in production or public models.
key_indicators: Use of exec() with remote content
Network request to external domain during deserialization
Code embedded in __reduce__ method of a custom class

execution_context.file_location: model weights file (PyTorch .bin or similar, serialized with pickle)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the custom ExecDict class abuses the __reduce__ method to execute the PAYLOAD (arbitrary code) when the model is unpickled, leading to code execution on the user's machine.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Overriding __reduce__ to execute code during unpickling is a classic technique for pickle-based code execution attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal __reduce__ methods should only control object reconstruction, not execute arbitrary code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Custom __reduce__ is used for advanced serialization, but never for code execution.
key_indicators: Embedding code execution logic in serialization hooks

attack_chain.action: User loads the model using from_pretrained, triggering unpickling of the model file.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary code execution via the __reduce__ method.

attack_chain.action: The PAYLOAD is executed, which fetches and runs remote code from pastebin.com.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution, potentially leading to further compromise (e.g., data exfiltration, malware installation).

behavioral_signatures: Arbitrary code execution during model loading/unpickling
Network requests initiated at import-time by model files
Presence of custom __reduce__ methods in serialized objects
file_indicators: PyTorch model files (.bin, .pt) containing custom class definitions with __reduce__
Model files that trigger unexpected network activity on load
network_indicators: Connections to pastebin.com or other code hosting services during model loading
Unexpected outbound HTTP requests from Python processes during deserialization
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python processes making network requests or executing code during model loading, scan model files for custom __reduce__ methods or embedded exec/eval calls, and use tools like Picklescan to analyze pickle files for unsafe code. Prefer loading models in the safetensors format, which does not allow code execution.
